Covered · Session 04M03

Conditional risk, expected value & simulation

Make decisions under uncertainty

Distinguish joint from conditional probability, compare payoffs across states, and inspect risk alongside averages.

Try this session’s experiment →
Study toolkitLaboratoryMind mapInfographicsListenFull slides
Updated study edition. This session uses the corrected 98-slide deck and corrected toolkit. Some references in the original lab package use the earlier slide numbering. Find the matching topic by title when the number differs. Assignment directions remain in Brightspace.

Read the session introduction →

What you can explain

  • Calculate conditional probability with the correct reference group.
  • Compare actions using expected value and downside.
  • Use simulation as a model-based experiment and test assumptions.

Name the reference group

Event A and B → P(A | B)

Conditional probability restricts the denominator to the condition. P(A | B) need not equal P(B | A). Base rates matter.

Connect it to a business example

A screen can detect most true cases while many positive screens are false alarms when the event is rare.

Choose across uncertain states

States → probabilities → payoffs → expected value

Expected value weights outcomes by probability. Probabilities sum to one, and payoffs use compatible units and horizons.

Connect it to a business example

Higher expected profit may come with a larger adverse-state loss. Compare both.

Model and simulate

Inputs → trial logic → outputs → sensitivity

Simulation explores assumptions. Its output is an estimate, not population truth. Inspect reproducibility and trial counts.

Connect it to a business example

Separate an analytic expectation from a particular run's mean. Check units, boundary inputs, and downside.

Communicate bounded risk

Expected result + downside + reversal condition

Explain which assumption could reverse the action. A fifth percentile is a cut-off with roughly 5% below it, not a guaranteed minimum.

Connect it to a business example

Name the threshold, loss risk, and next evidence before committing resources.
